chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked him about covered mosques, is standing in them disliked? He said, 'Yes, but prayer in them will not harm you today, and if justice were established, you would see for yourselves how it is done in that regard.' I asked him, 'Should a man hang his weapon in the mosque?' He said, 'Yes, but as for the Greater Mosque (Al-Masjid al-Akbar), no, for my father (peace be upon him) forbade a man from sharpening a scythe in the mosque.'

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The Greater Mosque (specifically referring to the mosque of Kufa in this context)
key_terms.جَدِّي: My father (referring to Imam Musa al-Kadhim)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in covered mosques and hanging weapons inside them according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while standing in covered mosques is technically disliked (makruh), the validity of prayer remains unaffected, noting that the current practice reflects a concession due to the absence of ideal conditions. He further distinguishes between general mosques, where hanging weapons is permitted, and the Greater Mosque (Masjid al-Haram), where it is prohibited, citing a precedent from his father, Imam al-Baqir, regarding the sharpening of a scythe to preserve the sanctity and cleanliness of the holy precinct.
